Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for New Zealand's reply. Some last words being spoken by Pat Cummins in the Australian huddle before they spread out to take their respective field positions. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Devon Conway and Will Young to open the innings for New Zealand. Mitchell Starc has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings for Australia. He has two slips in place to start with. Off we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Australia would have loved to cross 400 given the platform laid by the openers. However, the surface has shown signs of slowing up, meaning it should not be easy for New Zealand to chase this down. The Kiwi batters have a mountain to climb and if they pull this off, it will be the highest chase ever in ODI World Cup history. Do join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

Travis Head, the centurion is down for a chat. He says that it is nice to be back with the boys and get a game. On his hand, he says that it is doing nice and he is glad to be back. Mentions that it was a very good wicket and he and David Warner looked to take their chances and build a big partnership as well and 388 is a big score on the board. Adds that at the fag end of his innings, the ball did start to grip a bit and it was getting slightly harder to score with ease.

Having opted to bowl first, Tom Latham would have hoped his new-ball bowlers would be able to take advantage of the movement on offer early in the morning. It did not go according to plan for them, as both Trent Boult and Matt Henry were taken to the cleaners early on. It put them off their lines and lengths and leaked boundaries consistently. The third seamer, Lockie Ferguson, too, was taken for plenty in his first spell and could not bowl much to a right Achilles issue. As the field restrictions were lifted, spinners came on and Tom Latham quickly understood that it was the way to go on this surface which had started to slow up. Glenn Phillips led the fight back for New Zealand, accounting for Australia's top three batters and he found good support from Mitchell Santner who got into the act as well. At the start of the last 10 overs, New Zealand had high hopes of restricting Australia to an even lower total but they were stalled by cameos from Glenn Maxwell, Josh Inglis and Pat Cummins and dropping as many as 4 catches did not help either. That said, Trent Boult showed his class at the death with three wickets in the penultimate over before Matt Henry wrapped up the innings to keep New Zealand under 390.

After Australia were inserted into bat, it was a dream start for them. Returning to the side from an injury layoff, Travis Head set the tone for the Aussies and made his intentions clear right away. His opening partner, David Warner, followed suit and put the pressure back on the Kiwi pacers. The duo amassed 118 runs in the first powerplay and looked at utmost ease during the first ten overs. Warner got out on 81, but Head carried on and notched up a hundred on his World Cup debut. After the departure of the two openers, Mitchell Marsh was not able to continue the momentum, as was Steven Smith, and both departed trying to break the shackles. At 274-5, Australia seemed to be losing their way, but Glenn Maxwell scored 41 runs off just 24 balls to give his side some much-needed impetus. After that, it was absolute carnage from Josh Inglis and Pat Cummins with a 62-run stand which took Australia over 380. At that stage, they were on course for 400 but a flurry of wickets towards the end meant they had to settle for 388.

Australia have been bowled out for 388! Not many would have seen this coming when Pat Cummins and Josh Inglis were hitting boundaries for fun. The Aussies lose their last four wickets for just one run to be rolled over inside the 50 overs but this is still an imposing total. As far as New Zealand are concerned, they threw punches throughout to hang in there and have finished strongly with the ball.

Australia lose the last four wickets for just one run, getting bundled out in the process as well but they finish with a mammoth total of 388 runs on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match rituals and it is now time to get this Trans-Tasmanian rivalry underway! The two umpires and the Kiwi players take their positions on the field. And, it will be a rejuvenated Travis Head who will open the batting alongside an in-form David Warner for Australia. Matt Henry has the new ball in hand and is raring to make it talk. A couple of catchers in place in that slip cordon. Let's play...

We are inching closer to the first ball of the game but first, the two sets of players will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of New Zealand first followed by the national anthem of Australia.

Australia's captain Pat Cummins says that they are fine batting first. Mentions that it looks like a good wicket and it might have something early for the bowlers. Feels that the surface might slow up later. Informs that Travis Head returns to the side and Cameron Green is the unfortunate one to miss out.
